title: Contracting for Experimentation with Private Findings
abstract: arXiv:2611.01037v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A principal hires an agent to work on a project of unknown quality. Success is contractible, but before it occurs, the agent may privately obtain a favorable finding. For example, a scientist developing a drug may observe a promising microscope reading. An informed agent may conceal the finding; an uninformed agent may fake one. The agent's private information could guide both the project's duration and his pay. Yet I show that an optimal contract pays only success bonuses tied to time, not reported findings, consistent with time-based payment schedules often used in research funding. Dynamically arriving private information drives this simplicity: the agent can conceal good news to retain higher bonuses, so deterring concealment limits pay differences across report histories. translated_title: 针对带有私人发现的实验的合同设计
translated_abstract: 委托人雇佣代理人从事一个质量未知的项目。成功是可缔约验证的，但在成功发生之前，代理人可能会私下获得一个有利的发现。例如，开发药物的科学家可能观察到一份有前景的显微镜读数。知情的代理人可能会隐瞒这一发现；不知情的代理人则可能伪造发现。代理人的私人信息本可以同时指导项目的持续时间及其报酬。然而，我证明了最优合同只支付与时间挂钩的成功奖金，而不依据代理人报告的发现进行支付，这与科研资助中常用的基于时间的支付方案相一致。动态到达的私人信息推动了这种简单性：代理人可以隐瞒好消息以保留更高的奖金，因此阻止隐瞒行为限制了不同报告历史之间的报酬差异。奖金在诱导学习的研究阶段高且不断上升，随后在开发阶段降至一个较低且恒定的水平，在该阶段只有知情的代理人继续……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本文证明，当代理人在实验中可能私下获得并隐瞒有利发现时，最优合同只需支付与时间挂钩的成功奖金而无需依据报告的发现，从而解释了科研资助中基于时间的支付方案的合理性。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that when an agent may privately obtain and conceal favorable findings during experimentation, the optimal contract pays only time-based success bonuses rather than rewarding reported findings, rationalizing the time-based payment schedules commonly used in research funding.
